title: Adaptive span pruner with exporter hint propagation for OTLP -> backend exports
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: High-cardinality workloads are driving export costs and backend ingestion load. Many spans (e.g., debug-level, internal-sdk-heartbeats, transient retry spans) add noise but little value for latency/error dashboards. We need a safe, tenant-aware mechanism to prune low-value spans before they are sent to costly backends (Tempo/Jaeger) while preserving integrity for sampling and causal traces.

Goal: Implement an adaptive span pruner at the ingest layer that: (1) consumes exporter/tenant-level pruning hints (from console policies or automatic heuristics), (2) evaluates spans against lightweight rules and machine-learned scoring to drop or coalesce spans, (3) propagates metadata indicating pruned span ranges to downstream exporters for trace reconstruction/alerts, and (4) emits metrics and traces about pruning decisions for observability and audits.
acceptance_criteria: Configurable per-tenant pruning policy applied in the ingest path with zero-request path-change; admin config stored in console and available via config API
Integration with OTLP relay so exporters (Tempo/Jaeger) receive a ‘pruner-hint’ attribute when spans are dropped/coalesced
End-to-end test demonstrating 30-60% reduction in tokenized export size for a synthetic high-cardinality workload while maintaining >=95% fidelity on sampled tail traces
Dashboard showing pruning rate, false-positive alarms (user reports), per-tenant bytes saved, and latency impact introduced by the pruner
A safety override that prevents pruning for tenants with regulatory retention or for specific service-names/trace-ids
Documentation and runbook for rollback and investigation including a console flag to replay pruned spans from the ingest buffer for up to 24 hours
implementation_steps: Design: draft spec for hint propagation schema and pruner decision API (Confluence: /redwood/observability/pruner-spec)
Schema: add stable attribute 'pruner.hint' and 'pruner.dropped_count' to span envelope; document field semantics
Ingest hook: implement lightweight filter stage in edge-collector that applies tenant policy and scoring model; non-blocking and bounded CPU
Exporter integration: update OTLP relay to forward pruner attributes to Tempo/Jaeger adapters and add translation for Jaeger binary tags
Metrics: emit prometheus metrics (pruner_decisions_total, pruner_bytes_saved, pruner_processing_ms) and OpenTelemetry counters
Safety: implement bypass rules and add audit log entry for any pruned span set
Tests: build integration harness that replays golden traces and validates trace shape and tail-latency preservation
Docs + Runbook: write console UI copy, support troubleshooting steps, and a rollback playbook
notes:
Trade-offs considered: aggressive pruning reduces backend costs but increases risk of missing causal signals for debugging. We will start with tenant opt-in and conservative default rules (drop spans tagged sdk.debug=true and heartbeat spans older than 5s). Long-term: use a learned importance score that factors error/latency tags, span duration, and parent-child relationships.

Performance: implement pruner as a bounded worker pool with sampling fast-path using attribute-indexed hash checks to keep p95 processing latency <1ms. Any expensive scoring falls back to async tagging + replay buffer.

Storage: temporarily cache small batched span windows for 24h in a tenant-scoped ring buffer to allow replay on request (disk-backed, encrypted).
